chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Uqba, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! I have aged and weakened from fasting, so what should I do with these three days in every month?' He said, 'O Uqba, give in charity a dirham for each day.' I said, 'One dirham?' He said, 'Perhaps it is heavy for you, and you are belittling the dirham.' I said, 'The favors of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon me are abundant.' So he said, 'O Uqba, feeding a Muslim is better than fasting for a month.'

key_terms.قَضَاء: Redemption/Make-up (implied context of replacing missed fasts)

ai.seo_question: What is the alternative to fasting for the elderly or weak in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the specific case of an elderly or physically weak individual unable to fast, prescribing the redemption (*fidya*) of feeding a Muslim for each missed day. The Imam emphasizes the spiritual merit of this act by stating that feeding one Muslim is superior to fasting for an entire month, highlighting the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence between physical worship and charitable sustenance based on one's capacity. This ruling underscores the principle that ease is granted in religious obligations when hardship is present, a key tenet in Usul al-Fiqh.
